paper_metadata.title: Variational Quantum Monte Carlo Method with a Neural-Network Ansatz for Open Quantum Systems

summary: This paper presents a classical variational Monte Carlo method using a restricted Boltzmann machine density-matrix ansatz and stochastic reconfiguration to simulate the steady state of a dissipative 2D XYZ spin model. The authors show convergence toward exact results on small lattices, including 3x3 and 2x2 systems, with SR regularization parameters λ0 = 100, b = 0.998, and λmin = 0.01, but report no gate-based quantum hardware or quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Variational Monte Carlo simulation of the non-equilibrium steady state of a dissipative 2D XYZ spin model using a neural-network density-matrix ansatz (RBM) and stochastic reconfiguration; evaluated on small lattices against exact results.

algorithm.variant: Variational Monte Carlo with neural-network density-matrix ansatz (RBM) and stochastic reconfiguration
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterative SR updates until convergence of the Liouvillian expectation value / steady-state observables; no explicit stopping threshold reported

hyperparameters.alpha: M/N (hidden-node density), with alpha=beta in all calculations
hyperparameters.beta: L/N (hidden-node density), with alpha=beta in all calculations
hyperparameters.learning_rate_nu: small enough to guarantee convergence (exact value not reported)
hyperparameters.accepted_moves_target: roughly twice the number of variational parameters

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Parameters initialized to small random values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Spin-1/2 local degrees of freedom in the computational basis; density matrix represented over pairs of basis states |sigma>, |eta>
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find the non-equilibrium steady state rho_ss satisfying L(rho_ss)=0 by maximizing the real part of the Liouvillian expectation value / minimizing the Liouvillian residual in variational space
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Trace condition implied for steady-state density matrix; no explicit penalty formulation reported
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_<i,j> (Jx sigma_x^i sigma_x^j + Jy sigma_y^i sigma_y^j + Jz sigma_z^i sigma_z^j) with local dissipation via Lindblad jump operators sigma^-_k

problem_instance.description: Dissipative XYZ spin model on a 2D periodic lattice with local decay to |sigma_z=-1> steady state

dataset_specification.description: 2D spin lattices; explicit examples include 3x3, 2x2, and 3x3 systems

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared VMC observables against exact calculations; convergence shown as a function of alpha=beta and Jy/gamma; parameter sets in asymptotic SR region averaged over 100 samples

implementation_details.classical_solver: MINRES-QLP for the linear system in SR; Metropolis-Hastings sampling; CPU and GPU implementations
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Observables averaged over 100 parameter sets in the asymptotic SR region; exact comparison for small lattices

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Oscillatory at early times due to unitary part, then convergent

speedup_claims.caveats: No gate-based quantum speedup is claimed; the paper reports a classical variational Monte Carlo method. A GPU implementation is said to significantly speed up updates when the number of variational parameters is larger than 1000, but no quantitative speedup factor is reported.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(Np^3 + Np Nc) for evaluating SR quantities and Metropolis-Hastings sampling, as stated in the paper

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No quantum hardware resources reported; the paper uses classical CPU/GPU computation only.
